segments.text: American Fork City Council — Regular Session — June 23, 2026:

Daniel Swenson thanked the Council for stating that it would listen to community concerns regarding police conduct and referenced a recent public demonstration on the issue. He cited several incidents that he characterized as examples of police misconduct, including matters involving search warrants, traffic stops, residential encounters, and use-of-force allegations, some of which he noted are the subject of litigation. Mr. Swenson urged the City not only to listen to community concerns but also to implement meaningful changes to protect residents' rights.

Rod Martin, Chair of the American Fork Chamber of Commerce and a local business owner, expressed appreciation for the City's partnership with the Chamber in organizing Steel Days. He stated that the event has continued to grow through the efforts of businesses, volunteers, sponsors, City staff, and community members, and expressed confidence that the Chamber can continue to successfully manage the celebration. Mr. Martin also supported the use of appropriate conflict-of-interest safeguards, including recusal by elected officials who have professional relationships with the Chamber, to maintain transparency and public trust. He concluded by expressing appreciation for the City's police officers and encouraged the community to recognize the difficult nature of their work and extend them grace and support.

entities.speaker: Tim Holley
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Council Member Holley expressed concern that ongoing employee wage increases create long-term budget obligations that may necessitate future property tax increases. He stated that he would prefer to reevaluate some wage increases before delaying projects and reiterated that funding additional firefighter positions should be the City's highest budget priority. He also expressed concern that the interim budget tied the firefighter positions to approval of the proposed property tax increase and argued that the budget should communicate that public safety was the City's highest priority.

entities.speaker: Ryan Hunter
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Council Member Hunter emphasized that the interim budget included the firefighter positions and that the Council would determine final funding priorities during the Truth in Taxation process. He later stated that he believed there was sufficient Council support to fund the firefighter positions regardless of the final property-tax decision and that the budget could be amended if necessary.

entities.speaker: Staci Carroll
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Council Member Carroll stated that the proposed firefighter positions represented a new service expansion and were therefore appropriately identified as part of the proposed property-tax increase. She also noted that employee compensation increases reflected rising benefit costs as well as wages and emphasized the City's commitment to maintaining competitive compensation.

entities.speaker: Clark P. Taylor
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Council Member Taylor stated that he shared the goal of funding the firefighter positions but did not believe the interim budget language created the same concern. He stated that he intended to support funding the positions in the final budget.

entities.speaker: David H. Bunker
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Mr. Bunker explained that revenue associated with the proposed property-tax increase would be placed in a separate fund and could not be spent until after the Truth in Taxation hearing and adoption of the final budget. He said the interim budget preserved the Council's flexibility and that the final budget could be revised after the hearing to reflect its priorities, including reallocating funds to support firefighter positions.

entities.speaker: Anna Montoya
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Ms. Montoya clarified that the Council could amend any portion of the budget, including during final adoption after the Truth in Taxation hearing. She explained that the Council could adopt any tax rate up to the proposed maximum and that staff would revise the final budget accordingly.

entities.speaker: Ernie John
entities.remark-context: Interim budget and proposed property-tax increase

segments.text: Council Member John reaffirmed his support for ensuring that funding for public safety remained a priority while also emphasizing the importance of maintaining competitive wages to recruit and retain qualified City employees. He expressed confidence that the firefighter positions would be funded regardless of the final property-tax decision.
